label: downsize-cost-1921
_why: WHAT THE DOWNSIZING POLL COSTS LATE IN THE CENTURY. The user, 2026-10-30, put the poll into the basic telemetry stack; the play-time budget (§3.4) and every same-session wall-clock reading carry it from now on, so its tick cost is measured where it is largest: a 1921 world (~13,800 buildings in the vanilla save). Four continuations of ONE vanilla save (saves_debut 0336, 1921.1.1, the 20260807_005246 vanilla campaign), ALTERNATING the poll off and on, read with ledger/arm_tick_cost.mjs (the monthly pulse's hour-0 sub-tick of the 1st, where the poll runs, apart from the rest). Same start state for every run, so the arms differ by the poll and the seed's divergence only.

_arms.vanilla: {kind: control} - vanilla + the standard telemetry stack (country_state, population, tech_log, treasury, events, market_goods_scoped, the red-flag feed), downsize_feed false: no poll
_arms.vanilla_dz: {kind: control} - the same + the downsize feed (metric `downsizing`, telemetry v15)

_comparison: arm_tick_cost.mjs vanilla_dz against vanilla over 1921-1926 (2 runs an arm, alternating): the 1st-of-month hour-0 seconds a year, the rest, and the total; plus the poll's own DZM counts (tracked buildings a poll) and its DZ lines in the dz arm.
_predictions: The poll adds 0-2 s a year at the 1st-of-month sub-tick against ~100-150 s of play a year in 1921 (under 2%), the rest unchanged within the noise (the machine is in use: directional only, F258). Tracked a few hundred buildings a poll. Magnitude not argued.
